Operations review notes covering the full quarter as exported from the old wiki without formatting so everything runs together the warehouse team completed the racking reorganization in week two which freed up 340 square meters on the mezzanine level and reduced average pick path length by an estimated 18 percent although the measurement methodology changed mid-quarter so the comparison is indicative rather than exact the receiving dock schedule was rebuilt around the new carrier contract which moved the daily linehaul arrival from 6am to 4:30am and this required shifting two staff to the early window with the corresponding adjustment to the shift premium budget the returns processing backlog that built up during the February promotion was cleared by week five after the temporary staff authorization came through and the root cause analysis pointed to the label printer firmware rather than staffing levels which is why the printer fleet was upgraded in week seven at a cost of 12,400 euros against the 15,000 approved the inventory accuracy cycle counts ran at 99.2 percent for A items and 97.8 percent for B items both within target but the C item count slipped to 94.1 percent because the count team was pulled onto the returns backlog in weeks three and four and the recount is scheduled for the first week of next quarter the safety record shows two recordable incidents both minor hand injuries during the racking work and both closed with corrective actions around glove policy enforcement and the toolbox talk cadence was moved from monthly to biweekly as a result the energy consumption came in 7 percent under the same quarter last year attributed mostly to the LED retrofit completing in January and the dock door seal replacements reducing heating load the facilities team also flagged that the sprinkler inspection is due in the first month of next quarter and will require a four hour shutdown of the mezzanine level which needs to be coordinated with the pick schedule the transport damage rate held at 0.4 percent of shipped units against a 0.6 percent tolerance with the improvement credited to the new void fill machines and the retraining that followed the packaging audit the open actions carried into next quarter are the C item recount the sprinkler inspection shutdown the second phase of the racking plan for the ground floor and the carrier performance review which was deferred twice and is now flagged as at risk in the tracker.
